hist-ind-01-c2.text: Mark Cartwright (2023). Watt Steam Engine. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-ind-01-c2.quote: Thomas Newcomen (1664-1729), an ironmonger from Dartmouth, perfected his more powerful steam pump to drain coal mines of water in Dudley in the Midlands in 1712.
hist-ind-01-c2.claim: In 1712 Thomas Newcomen built a steam-powered pump for mines.

hist-ind-01-c2.text: Science Museum Group. Model Boulton and Watt condensing engine, c. 1800. Science Museum Group Collection.
hist-ind-01-c2.quote: This engine incorporates Watt's separate condenser (patented in 1769)
hist-ind-01-c2.claim: James Watt improved it in 1769 by adding a separate condenser

hist-ind-01-c2.text: Mark Cartwright (2023). Watt Steam Engine. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-ind-01-c2.quote: Watt and his business partner Matthew Boulton (1728-1809) made and sold almost 500 steam engines before their patent ran out in 1800
hist-ind-01-c2.claim: By 1800 there were roughly 500 Boulton & Watt engines operating across Britain, transforming industries from textiles to brewing.

hist-ind-02-c1.text: Mark Cartwright (2023). Stephenson's Rocket. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-ind-02-c1.quote: The Liverpool-Manchester line, the first inter-city service, opened on 15 September 1830 in the presence of no less a personage than a great war hero: the Duke of Wellington.
hist-ind-02-c1.claim: The Liverpool and Manchester Railway (1830), the world's first inter-city railway, opened the railway age.

hist-ind-02-c2.text: Mark Cartwright (2023). The Railways in the British Industrial Revolution. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-ind-02-c2.quote: The invention of mass-produced steel by Henry Bessemer (1813-1898) in 1856 allowed for rails that could carry heavier, more powerful, and faster trains
hist-ind-02-c2.claim: Henry Bessemer's converter (1856) made cheap steel possible for the first time, enabling railways, bridges, skyscrapers, and ships at scale.

hist-ind-06-c1.text: Mark Cartwright (2025). The Causes of WWI. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-ind-06-c1.quote: Germany as a state was born in 1871, following the Prussian victory over France in the Franco-Prussian War (1870-1) and the unification of the German states.
hist-ind-06-c1.claim: Germany unified in 1871 and industrialized rapidly under Bismarck and his successors.

hist-ind-07-c1.text: Mark Cartwright (2023). The Impact of the British Industrial Revolution. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-ind-07-c1.quote: The period between 1811 and 1816 saw the Luddites, named after their mythical leader Ned Ludd, smash factory machines.
hist-ind-07-c1.claim: Early responses included Luddite machinery breaking (1811-1816), strikes, mutual aid societies.
